name: Burj Khalifa
summary: Dubai's record-breaking tower rises from a three-winged plan around a central core. Its 828-metre architectural height makes it the tallest building in the world.

name: Merdeka Maybank Tower (Merdeka 118)
summary: Also known as Merdeka 118, this tower takes its name from the Malay word for independence and the neighbouring Stadium Merdeka. Its long spire helps it reach second place in the world rankings.
architect: Fender Katsalidis in association with RSP KL
style: Neo-futurism and Malay traditional songket pattern

name: Mecca Royal Clock Tower
summary: The centrepiece of a seven-tower hotel complex beside Mecca's Grand Mosque. Its enormous clock faces sit above the city, with a museum housed near the top.
architect: SL Rasch GmbH and Dar Al-Handasah Architects

name: Lotte World Tower
summary: South Korea's first building to pass 100 storeys combines homes, offices, shops and a hotel. A rooftop Sky Bridge tour takes visitors 541 metres above Seoul.

name: One World Trade Center
summary: The tower's symbolic 1,776-foot height recalls the year of American independence. It stands at the rebuilt World Trade Center, with an observatory above Lower Manhattan.

name: Taipei 101
summary: Taipei 101 held the world height record before Burj Khalifa. Its high-speed lifts once set their own record, whisking visitors from the fifth to the 89th floor in 37 seconds.

name: Central Park Tower
summary: The tallest residential building in the world. A cantilever on its east side opens Central Park views from the upper floors.

name: Lakhta Center
summary: Europe's tallest building rises on the outskirts of Saint Petersburg. Its twisting form also makes it one of the world's most northerly skyscrapers.

name: Landmark 81
summary: Vietnam's tallest building stands beside the Saigon River at the heart of Vinhomes Central Park. Its upper levels include a hotel and a multi-storey observation deck.

name: The Exchange 106
summary: This tower anchors Kuala Lumpur's Tun Razak Exchange financial district. It briefly overtook the Petronas Towers as Malaysia's tallest building before Merdeka 118 rose higher.
architect: Group Architects; Peter Chan (Architect of Record)

name: Petronas Tower 1
summary: One half of the Petronas pair that held the world height record from 1998 to 2004. Its steel-and-glass exterior and star-shaped floor plan draw on Islamic geometric motifs.

name: Petronas Tower 2
summary: The second of Kuala Lumpur's iconic Petronas twin towers shares a two-level skybridge with its neighbour. The pair remain the world's tallest twin skyscrapers.

name: Willis Tower
summary: Opened as the Sears Tower, this Chicago landmark held the world height record for nearly 25 years. Nine bundled structural tubes create its famous stepped silhouette.

name: Steinway Tower
summary: One of the most slender skyscrapers ever built, with terracotta and bronze bands on its facade. It rises behind the 1925 Steinway Hall.

name: One Vanderbilt
summary: Its tapering terracotta facade nods to the Chrysler Building nearby. An underground concourse links the tower directly to Grand Central.

name: 432 Park Avenue
summary: A slender concrete grid of identical square windows. Open floors every twelve storeys let wind pass through the tower.

name: Marina 101
summary: Marina 101 mixes hotel floors and apartments above Dubai Marina. Its long construction programme outlasted the original developer's funding, delaying the opening well beyond its initial schedule.

name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
summary: This glass tower stands beside the Chicago River, with a hotel below its residential floors. Adrian Smith designed it while at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill.

name: 270 Park Avenue
summary: JPMorganChase's headquarters stands on a fan-column base that lifts the tower above the street. It replaced the bank's earlier tower on the same site.

name: Princess Tower
summary: Princess Tower held the record for the world's tallest residential building from 2012 to 2015. Its Dubai Marina tower contains more than 760 homes above six basement levels.

name: Al Hamra Tower
summary: Kuwait's tallest building has an asymmetric form with tall flared walls. Glass wraps three sides, while the south-facing surface uses limestone to reduce exposure to the sun.

name: Haeundae LCT The Sharp Landmark Tower
summary: The tallest tower in a three-building complex facing Haeundae Beach. Its hotel and residences rise above shops, a spa and a water park, with an observatory on the 100th floor.
architect: Skidmore Owings & Merrill ; Samoo Architects & Engineers

name: Iconic Tower
summary: Africa's tallest building anchors the business district of Egypt's new capital. It is the centrepiece of a planned group of twenty towers, with most floors devoted to offices.

name: 23 Marina
summary: This slender residential tower stands at the northern end of Dubai Marina. Its 88 above-ground floors place homes almost 400 metres above the city.

name: 30 Hudson Yards
summary: The Edge observation deck projects from the 100th floor with a glass-floor viewing area. The tower belongs to the Hudson Yards development built above Manhattan's rail yards.

name: Public Investment Fund Tower
summary: The centrepiece of Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was designed by HOK and Omrania. Its TWIN lift system allows two cabins to operate in a single shaft.

name: Autograph Tower
summary: Autograph Tower is the centrepiece of Jakarta's Thamrin Nine development. Its height made it Indonesia's tallest building and a landmark of the Southern Hemisphere.

name: Burj Mohammed bin Rashid
summary: Abu Dhabi's tallest tower is the residential half of its World Trade Center complex. The development was reduced from three planned towers to two after the financial crisis.

name: Empire State Building
summary: Built in just over a year, it held the title of world's tallest building for nearly four decades. The antenna takes it to 443 m.

name: Elite Residence
summary: Elite Residence overlooks Palm Jumeirah from Dubai Marina. When completed in 2012, it ranked among the world's tallest residential buildings.

name: Ciel Dubai Marina
summary: Ciel Dubai Marina was designed as a supertall hotel overlooking the marina. Its 377-metre height puts it above Dubai's earlier record-setting hotel towers.

name: Federation Tower (East Tower)
summary: The eastern, taller half of Moscow's Federation Tower complex is also called Vostok. It took Europe's height record before Saint Petersburg's Lakhta Center surpassed it.

name: Kempinski The Boulevard Dubai
summary: Formerly Address Boulevard, this Downtown Dubai tower combines hotel rooms and residences. Its upper floors look towards Burj Khalifa, while the hotel includes three swimming pools.
architect: Atkins (concept) NORR Group Consultants International Ltd. (schematic, detailed design & record)

name: Bank of America Tower
summary: Faceted glass walls catch light from every direction. The tower was among the first skyscrapers designed to the highest green-building rating.

name: St. Regis Chicago
summary: Jeanne Gang's design stacks flowing, faceted sections above Chicago's Lakeshore East. On completion it became the world's tallest building designed by a woman.

name: Almas Tower
summary: Almas means diamond in Arabic, fitting a tower that houses Dubai's diamond-trading businesses. It stands on an artificial island within Jumeirah Lakes Towers.

name: City Tower 1
summary: City Tower One's deep facade grid and vertical sunshades give it a champagne-coloured finish. Its entrance screens draw on traditional mashrabiya patterns.

name: Gevora Hotel
summary: This gold-toned tower opened as the world's tallest hotel building in 2018. It contains 528 rooms and a swimming pool above its parking structure.

name: Il Primo Tower
summary: Il Primo rises beside Dubai Opera in the Downtown Opera District. Its residential floors were designed to take in views of Burj Khalifa and the surrounding landmarks.

name: JW Marriott Marquis Dubai Tower 1
summary: The first half of a twin-tower hotel complex with more than 1,600 rooms. Its faceted balconies and crown were inspired by the layered trunk of a date palm.

name: JW Marriott Marquis Dubai Tower 2
summary: The second tower completes the JW Marriott Marquis pair above Business Bay. Both concrete frames topped out in 2010, with the towers opening in separate phases.

name: Emirates Office Tower
summary: The office half of the Emirates Towers pair has a distinctive triangular plan. A retail boulevard connects it to its shorter hotel neighbour.

name: OKO – South Tower
summary: The taller, residential half of Moscow's OKO complex briefly held Europe's height record. Its name is both an old Russian word for eye and an abbreviation for the development's shared crystal base.

name: CBRT Tower
summary: Built for the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, this tower anchors Istanbul's Financial Center. It became the country's first supertall skyscraper.

name: The Marina Torch
summary: The Marina Torch briefly held the world's residential height record when it opened in 2011. Its crown makes it a recognisable part of Dubai Marina's dense cluster of towers.
architect: Khatib and Alami National Engineering Bureau

name: SkyTower at Pinnacle One Yonge
summary: SkyTower is the tallest element of the Pinnacle One Yonge development on Toronto's waterfront. Its planned height grew during development, with the project intended to become Canada's tallest residential building.

name: Chrysler Building
summary: The terraced stainless-steel crown made it the first building over 1,000 feet. It is still the tallest steel-framed brick building in the world.

name: 30 Rockefeller Plaza
summary: The centrepiece of Rockefeller Center and home to NBC's studios. The observation deck at the top is known as Top of the Rock.

name: MetLife Building
summary: Its broad octagonal slab straddles Park Avenue just north of Grand Central. It opened as the largest commercial office building in the world.
